chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from a man who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and complained to him of a pain in my body. So he said, 'Say, In the Name of Allah, then wipe your hand over it and say, I seek Refuge by the Might of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Majesty of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Magnificence of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Hold of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Messenger of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Names of Allah, from the evil of what I am cautious of, and from the evil of what I fear upon myself.' You should say it seven times.
He said, 'So I did it, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, removed the pain from me by it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for curing pain according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith illustrates the Shia practice of Ruqyah (spiritual healing) through the tactile application of divine names, emphasizing the interplay between physical action and spiritual invocation. The Imam’s instruction to wipe the affected area while reciting seeks refuge in Allah’s might, power, majesty, and greatness reflects a holistic approach to healing that integrates the believer's trust in God's attributes with tangible remedy. This specific supplication underscores the theological principle that healing comes solely from Allah, using His names as a means of seeking protection and relief from affliction.
